title: Volume
summary:
Volume is the total amount of exercise performed, considering frequency, intensity and duration. The chapter links adequate physical activity to a lower risk of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia and pregnancy-induced hypertension, better mood and energy, easier childbirth, and better postpartum recovery and weight management.

The general goal is at least 150 min of moderate-intensity activity per week in 20-30-min sessions on 3-5 days, combining aerobic, strength and flexibility work. Volume is then adjusted to prior activity level and health status, with specific ranges for sedentary, active and athlete women. Complications such as hypertension or gestational diabetes require adjusting volume under medical supervision.
points: Volume means the total exercise performed, combining frequency, intensity and duration.
The weekly goal is at least 150 min of moderate-intensity activity, in 20-30-min sessions on 3-5 days per week.
Programs should combine aerobic, strength and flexibility exercises.
Active women can keep a similar volume to before pregnancy, while sedentary women start lower and increase gradually.
With hypertension or gestational diabetes, volume must be adjusted under medical supervision.
Sedentary women are advised 90-150 min of moderate activity per week over 3-5 days, increasing with tolerance.
Active women can maintain a minimum of 150-300 min per week, without neglecting strength, balance, coordination and mobility.
Athletes can maintain 300 min or more per week, avoiding competitions or extreme training, with active recovery and vital sign monitoring.
Strength and core work should be moderate and progressive, and is especially important for sedentary women to prevent lower back pain and improve pelvic function.
takeaways: Spread activity over 3-5 days per week, depending on tolerance and trimester.
Build toward 150 min of moderate activity weekly.
Mix aerobic, strength and flexibility work.
Sedentary women should start with 90-150 min per week and increase slowly.
Add moderate, progressive strength and core training.
Review volume with your medical team as the pregnancy progresses.
cautions: With conditions such as hypertension or gestational diabetes, adjust volume only under medical supervision.
Athletes should avoid competitions or extreme training and keep constant medical supervision.
